subject: Deluxe Pack: metering, rounding, and minimums for hybrid token + seat bundle
messages:
From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@novaretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@novaretail.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on 'Deluxe Pack' metering for pilot

Irene — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Lydia and I reviewed the Deluxe Pack proposal (attached draft) and had a couple of billing questions before we finalize the pilot PO:

1) When you say “hybrid token + seat bundle” how are tokens accounted for across long contexts? Our app sends a ~6k token user context + a 512-token instruction; do we get billed on full context length or just generated tokens?

2) Rounding / minimums: the proposal mentions a 100-token minimum per request and a 1,000-token daily floor for the pilot. If we send many short calls (chat-like UX) will those be aggregated for rounding?

3) Reuse credits for prefix/kv caching: if we pin a 2k prefix and do many inference calls that reuse it, does Redwood provide any KV-reuse credit or is the full input counted each time?

Can we get a quick worked example on a few sample calls so we can map this to our analytics? Attached a small CSV with sample traffic.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20m call if easier.

–Tom
Head of Platform, NovaRetail

High level: NovaRetail wants explicit examples for a hybrid bundle that combines seats + committed token floor and also clear rules on aggregation/rounding and caching credits. Key items to confirm with product/pricing: 

- Definition of "context-billing" in Deluxe pack: whether input tokens are counted fully per call or partially credited when using prefix/KV reuse.
- Rounding window: are short requests aggregated per session, per minute, or per calendar day?
- Minimums interplay with seats: does a reserved seat allocation reduce token-floor billing?

Karthik — can you draft two worked examples (A: long-context read-heavy call; B: many small calls with heavy prefix reuse) with the current internal billing rules and a couple of alternative credit rules (e.g., 50% prefix credit; fixed prefix threshold) so we can propose a concession?

Vanessa — likely needs a one-time sales concession (discount or credit) to get pilot signed; can you indicate the approvable range for such a concession (%, or $ credit) so I can set expectations with the customer?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2025 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'Deluxe Pack' metering for pilot

Thanks — ran through the numbers. Below are two concrete worked examples and three alternate crediting models we can propose. I'm leaving the final concession numbers to Vanessa.

Assumptions (Deluxe pack baseline):
- Per-token billing: input + output tokens counted at 1 unit per token.
- Minimum per-call meter: 100 tokens (round up to 100).
- Daily floor: 1,000 tokens/day per account during pilot (billed if usage < floor).
- KV prefix reuse: no automatic credit (baseline).

Example A — Long-context single call (read-heavy)
- Request: 6,000-token context + 512-token instruction; model returns 300 tokens.
- Baseline billing: 6,512 input + 300 output = 6,812 tokens -> billed as 6,812 tokens.
- If we applied a "prefix partial-credit" (50% credit for pinned prefix up to 2k): credited amount = min(2,000, 6,000) * 50% = 1,000 tokens credit. Net billed = 6,812 - 1,000 = 5,812 tokens.

Example B — Many short calls with heavy prefix reuse (chat-like)
- Pattern: 200 calls/day; each call: 350-token prefix (same pinned prefix) + 200-token request + 60-token response = 610 tokens nominal per call.
- Baseline per-call rounding: each call >=100 so billed at 610 tokens. Daily total = 200 * 610 = 122,000 tokens.
- If we applied a session-aggregation window of 1 hour: aggregate tokens per session and round once per session. If 200 calls happen across 10 one-hour sessions evenly, per-session sum = 12,200 -> still >100 rounding irrelevant. Aggregation helps most when many very small calls right at the 100-minimum boundary.

Alternate crediting models we can offer (ranked by internal complexity):
1) Static prefix credit: first N tokens of any request (e.g., 500 tokens) are 50% credited when prefix matches. Simple to explain, cheap to compute.
2) KV-hit credit: if request hits cached KV entries, charge only for the deltas + output tokens. More accurate but requires tracing and higher infra accounting.
3) Session aggregation: aggregate calls within a 30- or 60-minute window and apply rounding once. Good for chat UX.

Impact on NovaRetail (quick numbers):
- Baseline projected monthly tokens (from attached CSV): ~12M tokens -> ~$X at list (calc in spreadsheet).
- With static prefix-credit (500@50%) we reduce bill by ~7-12% depending on their prefix magnitude.

Next steps: Vanessa — possible concession structures? Approvals needed: one-time pilot credit vs ongoing discount vs measured prefix-credit feature (engineering work).

—Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Billing
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'Deluxe Pack' metering for pilot

Good write-up. For a mid-market pilot like NovaRetail I can approve the following without exec sign-off:

- One-time pilot credit up to $10k (applied post-invoice) to cover any unexpected rounding/minimums in month 1.
- Up to a 10% recurring usage discount for the first 3 months if they commit to a minimum monthly seat + token floor (we should map seat counts to expected token usage so discount preserves unit economics).
- For engineered prefix-credit (KV-hit credit), we need an SOW with product; that is multi-quarter and should be treated as roadmap/PS work, not a billing concession.

Ask: Irene, please confirm the pilot term (30 days?) and whether NovaRetail prefers a dollar credit or percentage rebate; I'll allocate the $10k pilot bucket if they want the dollar approach. Also need expected renewal date to size the discount.

—Vanessa
Head of Revenue Operations

Subject: Re: Question on 'Deluxe Pack' metering for pilot

Tom / Lydia — thanks for the note and for the sample traffic. We've reviewed internally and can offer a pilot structure that addresses your main concerns while keeping billing predictable:

Summary offer for 30-day pilot:
- Billing rule: baseline counts input + output tokens per call.
- Aggregation: we'll aggregate short calls within 60-minute windows for rounding purposes (helps many small chat calls).
- Prefix/KV reuse: we'll apply a static prefix credit = 500 tokens @ 50% for pinned prefixes (no infra changes required).
- Minimums: 100-token per-call rounding still applies; 1,000 daily floor retained for the pilot but we will apply a one-time pilot credit up to $10,000 to cover month-1 overages if your real usage falls below expected profile.
- Discount: if you sign a 3-month committed pilot (seat + token floor) we'll extend a 10% recurring usage discount for months 2–4.

Worked examples are attached (calculation_examples.csv) and I've included the revised proposal (novaretail_deluxe_proposal_v2.xlsx) with the concession highlighted.

If that sounds reasonable I can send a short amendment to the SOW and we can kick off billing changes. Happy to do a 20m call today at 4:30p PT to walk through the calc.

Best,
Irene
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
